summary: The translation is faithful in most of the paragraph, but it misreads אל in קורין אל as the name God (2:28.463-464), garbles שם 'there' at 2:28.565, renders להשפיע as 'prayer bestows', makes the sages' clause (אשר ... אושרו) refer to 'errors', and leaves two sentence fragments and several lower-case sentence starts. Ten verse allusions were missing from apparatus (Esth 7:5 among them). The unresolved words are decided from context: Mesharef is the questioner's pun on the title Metzaref ha-Emunah (3:10, 3:12); תשבורת and תוכנים are mathematics and astronomy; מערב is the Maghreb; ומונים stays 'multitudes'. Patches correct the English, phrases, literal, grammar, apparatus and the affected tokens.

patches.value: Reply. To man the arrangements of the heart, and from the LORD the answer of the tongue. And it was when I saw your letter, I sat astonished and dismayed. How your heart emboldened you to inquire and investigate after the band of the Geonim, who are faithful in the Torah, distinguished in lineage, like the seed of the mighty, and after several decisors and also expounders, the early and the later, the sages of the Maghreb, Ashkenaz, Sefarad and the Yemenites. And the rest of the congregations, the holy seed, the faithful children, this is their treasure, more than fine gold and many pearls. Can a stumbling come from the hand of righteous and faithful ones, who know knowledge, the wise and discerning, who fear God and turn aside from evil with their might. By their wisdom they felled many foes and multitudes who stood against them in every age. Can it be that their Kabbalah is compounded in vanity and errors, they who, because of their great wisdom, were approved by the mouths of princes and nobles and stood before kings and rulers, and can fathers and sons walk on a path that is not good? How many hundreds of years is this? And how many of them are distinguished in every wisdom, and scholars, Kabbalists with philosophy and logic, medicine, mathematics and astronomy, meditating day and night, quiet and at ease, eating the good fruit of their deeds, fat and lush. Heaven forbid! This is not to be believed and does not come to mind except to the simple, who believe every word, who lean on their understanding. And properly, it is not incumbent on me to answer you. For what am I, to enter the innermost, into what I was not permitted to ponder, all the more so to answer questioners. But because it is a time to act for the LORD, I answer you from what I found written in the words of our Sages of blessed memory. May their merit stand for me, that no stumbling befall through me. Now, as for what you wrote, that you do not despise the sages of Israel, there are already several witnesses against you; you cannot deny it. And as for what brought you to this, that you attribute to them error and heresy: it is only because they are despised in your eyes. But a person should take heed for himself, lest he be burned by their coals, for the righteous are greater in their death than in their life, as they said in the Talmud. And as for what you wrote, that if one reveals the place of contradiction, and the Talmud also brings proof to refute the words of those greater than them, the case is not comparable to the proof, for where do we find that they bring proof to refute a halakhah given to Moses at Sinai? And the sages of Kabbalah say that thus they received from the mouth of Moses, and who is this one, and where is he, who gave you permission to inquire and investigate after their words? And as for what you wrote, that they call the partzufim divinities, God forbid, that they say thus. And as for what you wrote, go and learn from the intention of the blessings and the prayers. They already explained that the Cause of all causes is designated in a certain sefirah by such a name, and in a certain sefirah by that name. And as for what you wrote, that the Kabbalists explained that there are several worlds, thousands of thousands, etc., even if they were millions of millions, since they say that their Creator is one, and He gives life to all of them: what loss is there from this? And as for what you wrote, that they are in the image of a man possessing stature, already they said, "Great is the power of the prophets, who liken the likeness of the Power above to the form of a man." And as for what you wrote about 248 limbs, they already explained what the limbs are. For they are 216 letters of the Name of 72 and 32 paths, which allude to divine powers. And as for what you wrote, that I already conceded that my opinion is that there is no prayer applicable to the Cause of all causes, you speak falsehood. But surely, from the beginning of your question to me about the words of the Mesharef, I answered you, see in Kisse Eliyahu. But our Kabbalah holds that prayer is to Ein Sof and to bestow the flow upon the ten sefirot, as Lechem Shelomo wrote. And as for what I told you, to consult Kisse Eliyahu, so that you would know that the words of the Mesharef are words of heresy, in truth, and fitting to root it out. And God forbid that there be found in any book words like his, but the words of Kisse Eliyahu are not like his, God forbid. For the words of Kisse Eliyahu hold that Ze'ir Anpin is nothing but a vessel for the action of the Creator. And as for what he wrote on folio 25, that when we call upon Ze'ir Anpin, we call upon all the partzufim, with a soul hidden in them, which is Ein Sof, blessed be He. This does not mean that prayer is not directed to Ein Sof, Heaven forbid, but it means that the ascent of prayer to Ein Sof, blessed be He, is by way of this attribute. And the proof for this is what he wrote on folio 17b, and these are his words: "As for what is written about the intentions of prayer and the blessings, to direct in each blessing a particular intention, to a particular sefirah, not, God forbid, to the essence of the sefirah. For it is a cutting off, God forbid, and Heaven forbid to direct it to any particular power or particular sefirah. But all is to the essence of the one Ein Sof, blessed be He, the totality of all the powers, all of them." And furthermore he wrote on folio 25a: "And all our prayers are to Ein Sof, may He be blessed. Except that we cannot call Him by any appellation and name. Therefore we pray through the sefirot. For there is the applicability of all, all the appellations and names. For all the appellations and names are names of His essence, extending through the sefirot." Also he wrote on folio 26: "And if they do not do so, and do not dedicate their prayer solely to Ze'ir Anpin, they will not be answered." And all the Kabbalists lay down this principle, and these are their words: "As for whatever you find in some book of theirs, that prayer is addressed to any sefirah, Heaven forbid that it be so. But the intention is that one intend to raise them to Ein Sof by way of that sefirah."
patches.reason: Fidelity and English: אל in קורין אל is 'to', so 'call upon', not 'call God' (2:28.463-464); שם at 2:28.565 is 'there' and the sentence was garbled; מלאך לבך lacks its object 'you' (Esth 7:5); אושרו has the sages as subject, not 'errors'; להשפיע is not 'prayer bestows'; ייחדו with אלא is 'dedicate ... solely'; the fragment 'Rather, because' joined by a colon per the fragment ruling; 'Cause of all causes' capitalised per the epithet ruling; הנדון is 'the case'; חכמי is 'sages'; the Midrashic saying has גבורה = the Power, דמות = likeness; sentence starts capitalised; verses (Prov 14:15, Ps 19:11, Ps 92:15) govern wording; 'the innermost' for the idiom; the participial passage joined to the list of sciences.

value: The paragraph is the respondent's reply in chapter 2. "You" is the questioner; the reply takes up each point of his letter in turn, introduced by ומה שכתבת ("as for what you wrote") and answered after it.

The rhetorical questions opened by וכי ("Can it be that ...", 2:28.56, 2:28.80, 2:28.96) and the sentences ending in a question mark (2:28.102, 2:28.106, 2:28.260, 2:28.279, 2:28.337) keep their question form; the text gives no answer to them within the paragraph.

Quotations of the Kabbalists are in double quotation marks. They open after the formula וז"ל (2:28.501, 2:28.601) or after כ' with a folio (2:28.539, 2:28.580), and close at the end of each passage, since the text gives no closing formula. The quoted words are Hebrew, except כיילי כללא דא (2:28.598-600), which is Aramaic and is rendered by its sense.

The verb ייחדו (2:28.589) is rendered "dedicate": to set the prayer apart for one addressee, the sense that fits אלא ("only"). "Unify" in the Kabbalistic sense is the alternative (see the review question); לז"א (2:28.592) is the entity the prayer is dedicated to.
Two Biblical allusions carry the opening and the close of the argument: Prov 16:1 at the start (2:28.1-7), and the word לה' from Ps 119:126 (2:28.172), which the author reads as "for the LORD".

אין הנדון דומה לראיה (2:28.249-252) is a fixed idiom of argument: the case under discussion is not like the case cited as proof, so the proof does not apply. לפני ולפנים (2:28.158-159) is the idiom for the innermost part (of the Temple), literally "before and within".
patches.reason: ייחדו note corrected; idioms הנדון and לפני ולפנים added.

value: Base text: Wikisource, as printed; the 1931 scan is not yet collated (Q2), so no reading is added or corrected here.

Prov 16:1 (allusion at the opening, 2:28.1-7): the verse reads "The arrangements of the heart belong to man, and the answer of the tongue is from the LORD." The author's Hebrew is the verse's words with תשובה prefixed.
Job 1:1 (allusion, 2:28.66-70): "וִירֵא אֱלֹהִים וְסָר מֵרָע", rendered "fear God and turn from evil", with the author's plural form.
Isa 6:13 (allusion, 2:28.46-47): "זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ", "the holy seed".
Isa 65:2 (allusion, 2:28.97-100): "בְּדֶרֶךְ לֹא־טוֹב", "in a way that is not good".
Ps 92:15 (allusion, 2:28.129-130): "דְּשֵׁנִים וְרַעֲנַנִּים", "fat and luxuriant".
Avot 2:10 (allusion, 2:28.224-225): the author's "פן יכוה בגחלתן" recalls the saying to beware of the coals of the sages; the words are his, not a quotation.
Ps 119:126 (allusion, 2:28.171-172): "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה'", "It is a time to act for the LORD".
Folio references as the author gives them: folio 17b (2:28.498-500), folio 25 (2:28.458-459, 2:28.541-543), folio 26 (2:28.582-583). No reference is added.
The doubled "כל כל" (2:28.567-568) is as printed; both words are translated.

ומונים (2:28.75): the word is uncertain. Read as והמונים with the ה dropped ("multitudes", rhyming with the -ים series); the alternative is a misprint for ומינים ("and heretics"). Rendered "and multitudes".

המשרף (2:28.402, 2:28.427): not a person here. In 3:10 and 3:12 the questioner is charged with calling the book Metzaref ha-Emunah ("Refiner of Faith") "the book Mesharef" and "Mesharef ha-Emunah" ("Burner of Faith"), from שרף "burn": a play on מצרף. The transliteration "Mesharef" is kept.

ותשבורת and ותוכנים (2:28.118-119): names of sciences in a list with medicine. תשבורת (cf. "חכמת התשבורת בשמים ובארץ", 4:27, with חשבון, 8:11) is mensuration, mathematics; תוכנים is the plural of תכונה, astronomy. Rendered "mathematics and astronomy".
The Talmudic sayings (2:28.233-234, 2:28.241-260, 2:28.258-260) are given without a reference, since the author gives none.

Esth 7:5 (allusion, 2:28.15-17): "אֲשֶׁר מְלָאוֹ לִבּוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן", "whose heart has emboldened him to do so"; again at 2:28.268-273, "מִי הוּא זֶה וְאֵי זֶה הוּא", "who is this one, and where is he".
Ezra 9:3 (allusion, 2:28.12-13): "וָאֵשְׁבָה מְשׁוֹמֵם", "and I sat appalled".
1 Sam 10:5 (allusion, 2:28.21): "חֶבֶל נְבִיאִים", "a band of prophets".
Prov 22:29 (allusion, 2:28.92-94): "לִפְנֵי מְלָכִים יִתְיַצָּב", "he shall stand before kings".
Ps 19:11 and Prov 3:15 (allusion, 2:28.52-55): "הַנֶּחֱמָדִים מִזָּהָב וּמִפַּז רָב", "more desirable than gold, than much fine gold"; "יְקָרָה הִיא מִפְּנִינִים", "more precious than pearls".
Ps 1:2 and Josh 1:8 (allusion, 2:28.120-122): "יֶהְגֶּה יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה", "he meditates day and night".
Jer 46:27 and 30:10 (allusion, 2:28.123-124): "וְשָׁקֵט וְשַׁאֲנָן", "quiet and at ease".
Isa 3:10 (allusion, 2:28.125-127): "פְּרִי מַעַלְלֵיהֶם יֹאכֵלוּ", "they shall eat the fruit of their deeds".
Prov 14:15 (allusion, 2:28.141-144): "פֶּתִי יַאֲמִין לְכָל דָּבָר", "the simple believes every word".
Neh 9:6 (allusion, 2:28.330-333): "וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם", "and You give life to all of them".
שם (2:28.565): read "there" (in the sefirot, where the epithets apply); the alternative is "the name".
patches.reason: Missing allusions listed (Esth 7:5, Ezra 9:3, 1 Sam 10:5, Prov 22:29, Ps 19:11, Ps 1:2, Jer 46:27, Isa 3:10, Prov 14:15, Neh 9:6); notes on המשרף, ומונים, תשבורת/תוכנים rewritten from the corpus; שם recorded.
מלאך = מלא + ך, with the object 'you' (Esth 7:5).

patches.value: מלאך: "has filled you", i.e. emboldened you, after Esth 7:5 (see apparatus).
patches.reason: The note explains the verb with its object.

patches.value: האיתנים: "the mighty, the enduring"; the Sages read האיתנים in Mic 6:2 as the patriarchs (Rosh Hashanah 11a), so "seed of the mighty" may mean the descendants of the patriarchs.

patches.reason: מערב in a list of communities with Ashkenaz, Sefarad and Yemen is the usual Hebrew name of North Africa (Arabic Maghrib, 'the West'); proposed ruling: "the Maghreb", with "the West" in the note. The rulings are silent.

patches.value: מערב: literally "the West"; in a list of communities the usual Hebrew name of North Africa (the Maghreb).
ומונים: read as והמונים, "multitudes", with the ה dropped; the alternative is a misprint for ומינים, "heretics". Rendered "and multitudes" (see apparatus).
patches.reason: Rulings silent; proposed: keep "multitudes", record ומינים as the alternative.
אשר here refers to the sages (plural אושרו, התיצבו), not to the errors.

patches.value: מקובלים: "Kabbalists"; the participle can also mean "accepted, esteemed" ("esteemed with philosophy and logic").
patches.reason: Ambiguous word flagged for the learner.
From the corpus: חכמת התשבורת בשמים ובארץ (4:27), חשבון ותשבורת (8:11): mensuration, mathematics. Rulings silent; proposed "mathematics".

patches.value: ותשבורת: a medieval Hebrew name for mathematics, mensuration (cf. 4:27, 8:11).

patches.reason: תוכנים is the plural of תכונה, the medieval Hebrew word for astronomy; the list is of sciences. Proposed "astronomy", not "computations".

patches.value: הוגים: the participle continues the preceding sentence (a Hebrew full stop precedes it); joined by a comma in English because it has no main clause. Echoes Ps 1:2.
לפני ולפנים: the idiom for the innermost part (literally "before and within").

patches.reason: הנדון is the case under discussion, not 'the matter'.

patches.value: הנדון: "the case under discussion"; אין הנדון דומה לראיה: the case is not like the proof cited.
הקבלה: "Kabbalah", the Kabbalists' lore; here the Kabbalists themselves claim a tradition from Moses.
patches.reason: The old note put the author's claim on the word in the mouth of this respondent.
גבורה as a name of God ('the Power'), not 'might'.

patches.value: המשרף: "the Mesharef", from שרף "burn"; in 3:10 and 3:12 the name the questioner is said to have given the book Metzaref ha-Emunah ("Refiner of Faith"), a play on מצרף (see apparatus).
patches.reason: Rulings silent on the name. Proposed: keep the transliteration "the Mesharef" with this note.
להשפיע is an infinitive; prayer does not itself bestow.

patches.value: ולהשפיע: "and to bestow the flow"; the infinitive continues לא"ס (prayer is to Ein Sof and to bring the flow to the sefirot).
אל: the preposition (קורין אל, "call upon"), not the name El.
patches.reason: The old note read it as God.

patches.value: קיצוץ: "cutting off", the charge of severing the sefirot from their source.

patches.reason: שם = 'there' (in the sefirot); 'the name' made the sentence unintelligible.

patches.value: שם: "there"; the alternative "the name" is in apparatus.

patches.reason: ייחד with אלא is 'dedicate solely'; 'unify' is the Kabbalistic alternative. Proposed ruling: "dedicate".

patches.value: ייחדו: "dedicate" (to set apart for one addressee); the alternative is the Kabbalistic "unify".
כיילי: Aramaic, "they formulate, lay down", with כללא דא "this rule".
